summary: Keep exact-revision mission runs pinned across head publications and retries

replay.detail: New mission-run.created claims retain optional top-level revision_pinned body metadata, covered by both the claim content hash and the signature content digest. It cannot be stripped or changed in transit without invalidating authentication. Readers derive legacy uses-mission pin intent from the immutable parent step generation; incremental replay, full replay and refold use the same claim-based reader, never wall-clock time or current head to infer pins. Historical standalone explicit-revision requests are indistinguishable from head-following requests and retain the previous behavior.

schema.detail: Optional signed body metadata outside fields; no claim registry, storage schema, public client-v0 model, schema document or generated-client change. Declarative mission-run creation accepts follow-head "true" alongside an exact admission revision, distinguishing internally resolved selection from an explicit revision pin.

rules.detail: Automatic restart-active and when-idle head supersession exclude exact-revision runs. Default retries retain a pinned source revision. Explicit authorized revision adoption is unchanged. CLI starts without --revision emit follow-head "true" so internal head resolution does not pin the run. Declarative starts default to pinned unless follow-head is requested. Unpinned runs and their automatic successors continue following head publications.

compatibility.detail: The daemon advertises mission_run_follow_head=1 in /v1/health. The CLI emits follow-head only when that capability is advertised; absent or zero capabilities retain the old exact declaration, allowing starts against older daemons even though those runs may be recorded as pinned. Declarative authors using follow-head must publish to an upgraded daemon. Encoding the pin inside fields would cause old peers to retain the creation record as unknown and leave it unprojected. Top-level body metadata instead follows the existing signed-metadata convention: old peers validate the unchanged fields schema, admit the claim and ignore the metadata. They can still retarget pinned runs. Automatic publication supersession executes on the daemon whose store origin authored mission-run.created, not necessarily the publisher or a read replica. Upgrade every run-owning daemon before resuming publications or reconciliation; upgrading only the publishing daemon is insufficient.

downtime.detail: Normal binary restart only; no database migration.

manual.detail: Already superseded runs are not repaired or resurrected. Stop incorrect live replacements and explicitly start the originally intended revision through the authorized workflow, restoring any parent linkage through that workflow rather than editing claims. Historical standalone pinned runs need an explicit replacement with recorded pin intent if they must be protected.

recovery.detail: Rollback restores the old automatic supersession behavior, including on claims carrying revision_pinned. Keep publication and execution paused on older run owners if pin preservation is required.
